messages:
maria.support: Customer ticket #C-4821 — structured output mode returning JSON that our SDK/json parser rejects. Customer sees a parse error: 'Unexpected control character at position 482'. They attached the raw response.

maria.support: Request ID: req_0a7f9b2d. SDK: nodejs@2.3.1, using structured_output=true.

maria.support: Raw response (copied from capture):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "{\\"summary\\": \\\"Customer reported parsing error\\\", \\\"details\\\": \\\"Line1\\u000BLine2\\\"}"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

maria.support: Note the inner JSON string contains a literal vertical tab escape `\u000B` (or in some captures it shows as an actual VT char). The customer's JSON.parse throws when we pass through our SDK streaming aggregator.

megan.backend: Can you paste the minimal prompt + params you used to reproduce? Is structured_output the model-side JSON or our post-processing?

maria.support: Repro steps I ran:
1) POST /v1/responses with body:
```json
{
  "model": "open-instruct-2025",
  "input": "Summarize: Keep output as a JSON string field called result. Include a line break and a vertical-tab between lines.",
  "structured_output": true
}
```
2) Capture body from response stream (we just concat chunks) and call JSON.parse on the top-level body. Fails ~60% of runs.

jay.ml: This smells like two separate issues: a) Model sometimes emits literal control chars (U+000B, U+000C) inside strings when asked to include weird separators. b) Our stream aggregator doesn't normalize non-standard separators before handing to JSON.parse. If the stream boundary cuts inside a surrogate/escape sequence we can end up with truncated `\u` escapes.

jay.ml: Example of problematic chunking: chunk1 ends with `\\u00` and chunk2 starts with `0B"}` -> when joined naively it's fine, but if we do incremental parse attempts we might try to parse chunk1 alone and fail. Any streaming parse attempt needs to buffer until complete.

bob.infra: deploy-bot noted we rolled runtime inference v3.7.2 ~ 1860000200 that changed streaming buffer flush behavior (flush on token not on character). Might be related.

deploy-bot: [deploy] runtime-inference v3.7.2 deployed to prod-us-west at 1860000200 by @bob.infra.

megan.backend: Good catch. Two actions: 1) Add sanitizer in SDK for structured_output mode that escapes control chars (replace U+0000–U+001F except common ones with unicode-escaped \u00XX). 2) Add protective buffering in the stream reassembler: do not attempt to parse until final `}` of top-level JSON is seen or a matching bracket depth returns to 0.

maria.support: I can push a quick SDK workaround to customer (escape control chars) and ask them to upgrade. Also cc'ing customer success.

jay.ml: Long-term we should: a) update model safety/eval to test for control-char emissions in structured outputs, b) add a server-side sanitizer toggle for enterprise/private deployments (opt-in), c) revert or patch v3.7.2 streaming flush if that's the root.

bob.infra: I'll roll a small patch to the stream reassembler to avoid incremental parse attempts and increase buffer window for 2 releases. If that doesn't resolve, we'll consider rollback.

maria.support: Marking ticket P1 for now until we confirm customer can parse after SDK workaround. Will update status in the ticket. :thumbsup:

megan.backend: Thx — if anyone needs logs for req_0a7f9b2d I uploaded them to the incident bucket (s3://redwood-support/repro/req_0a7f9b2d.log).

maria.support: ETA to customer reply: EOD.

jay.ml: Quick note: also watch for ZERO WIDTH JOINER (U+200D) and other ZW* chars — they can be invisible in logs and still change tokenization. Might explain some intermittent cases.

maria.support: Adding that to the bug notes.
